criteria.rationale: Checked L1 and L2 against code. L2 holds: accepted limits enter digestReviewPlan and reviewBundlePlanDigest. L1 is justified for how broad or weak a limit is written, not for the engine cutting it (N1). review-check warns the sealed evidence is current by provenance rather than run on the subject head; local focused tests of the scope passed.
The change adds pure parsing, digest fields and a bounded file read; no shared state or new goroutine in production code.
Unsealed limit and blank reason are refused with named blockers; ADR reads are bounded and fail closed. The parser gap is recorded under correctness.
Refusals name the finding and limit; the attestation records limit and reason. The stats gap is N5.

accepted_limits and limit are omitempty in plan, bundle, draft and finding and in both plan digests; the bundle digest test compares with the earlier struct; earlier brief templates render without the new section and the digest tests pass.

D1 and D2 address the cause, no place to declare an assumed environment: limits are sealed from the spec, listed in the brief and judged from the bundle, with a separate disposition that needs a sealed id. The design assessment reports no structural delta.
The scope change sets match R1 to R4 and the declared artifacts; no cap on rounds was added. The brief template file also carries earlier versions belonging to other specs in the range.

within-limit requires an id sealed in the bundle and a non-blank reason; a run attestation must match the draft; the manual attest syntax cannot set a limit; brief text is flattened by quoteLedgerText; ADR reads do not follow file links. Fidelity of the sealed text is N1 and N2.

One section, one optional field and one disposition is close to the smallest way to classify findings; an accepted-risk reuse would have lifted its severity bound. The choice fails if limits cannot be read faithfully, which N1 shows needs fixing.
